--- title: "Initial syllable matching" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_INICIAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_INICIAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Emparejar sílaba inicial*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_INICIAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Initial syllable matching, from age 4 to 5 (6,550 administrations in 6 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .39. AUC .61–.67 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 525 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 5 (525) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child selects from an array of three pictures the one whose name starts with the same syllable as the object depicted above. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:-------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------------:| | 525|Identificar sílabas |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla | 5| 1|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5, 5.1| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **525.** 1 ejemplo + 5 ítems: una imagen arriba y tres opciones. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![525 · Identificar sílabas](../../figuras/plataforma/525.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 525"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](../CF523.en.qmd) and [rapid naming](../RAN.en.qmd). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2011| 67|2015/16 | 931| 0| 931| 34| | 4.1| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 387| 387| 0| 17| | 4.1| 2013| 181|2017/18 | 572| 565| 7| 24| | 4.1| 2014| 625|2018/19 | 446| 49| 397| 20| | 4.1| 2015| 894|2019/20 | 488| 0| 488| 22| | 4.2| 2014| 626|2018/19 | 389| 6| 383| 20| | 4.3| 2014| 627|2018/19 | 385| 0| 385| 20| | 5.1| 2010| 66|2015/16 | 956| 260| 694| 36| | 5.1| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 903| 0| 903| 34| | 5.1| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 319| 315| 0| 16| | 5.1| 2013| 628|2018/19 | 774| 511| 263| 33| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|-----:|----------------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 1,001| 2012, 2013, 2014| 3.56| 1.63| 4| -0.19| 3.70| 14.29| | 5.1| 1,086| 2010, 2012, 2013| 4.73| 1.44| 5| -1.01| 0.46| 42.17| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–6 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|-----:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 4.1| 1,001|0–6 |0–6 |0–6 | | | 5.1| 1,086|1–6 |0–6 |0–6 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .27–.52 (median .39, 6 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .63. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2011| 4.1| 5.1| 805| 0.25| 0.27| | 2012| 4.1| 5.1| 305| 0.35| 0.38| | 2013| 4.1| 5.1| 397| 0.32| 0.33| | 2014| 4.1| 4.2| 365| 0.46| 0.47| | 2014| 4.1| 4.3| 368| 0.39| 0.40| | 2014| 4.2| 4.3| 373| 0.52| 0.52| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .40–.52. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (4.1, r = .32); Oral morphosyntax (4.2, r = .36); Letter knowledge (4.3, r = .28); Letter knowledge (5.1, r = .39). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .61–.67. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.62. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_INICIAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .61–.62 (2 time points; 470–767 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|-----:|----------------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 1,001| 2012, 2013, 2014| 1| 2| 2| 2| 4| 5| 6| | 4.2| 389| 2014| 2| 2| 3| 4| 5| 6| 6| | 4.3| 385| 2014| 2| 2| 3| 4| 5| 6| 6| | 5.1| 1,086| 2010, 2012, 2013| 2| 2| 3| 4| 5| 6| 6| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_EMPAREJA_SILABA_INICIAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 2,478| 0.030| 0.138| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 2,646| -0.002| 0.950| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 2,663| 0.186| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 2,824| 0.083| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 352| 0.149| 0.005| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 339| 0.080| 0.460| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 363| 0.150| 0.004| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 389| 0.133| | |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 356| 0.082| 0.123| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 341| 0.118| 0.280| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 365| 0.087| 0.097| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 385| 0.117| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 2,840| 0.048| 0.011| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 2,792| -0.048| 0.202| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 2,785| 0.118| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 2,952| 0.077| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Initial syllable matching” (code 525; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (initial syllable identification). The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It comprises 6 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 11 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .63 (N = 2,220, 6 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 12 months) was ρ = .37 (median of 5 session pairs; range .27–.52). Stability across time points was ρ = .27–.52. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.62. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.1 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
